Emergencies: SVC obstruction, spinal cord compression, hypercalcaemia, massive haemoptysis, tracheal obstruction.
Neurological: Neck stiffness, altered mental status, focal neurological deficits (meningeal TB, spinal cord compression).
Presence of complications: Massive haemoptysis, respiratory failure, spinal cord compression, neurological deficits, cardiac tamponade.
Pathologic fractures / spinal cord compression: Focal bone pain, neurologic deficit — Orthopaedic fixation or radiotherapy, continue systemic therapy, immobilise
Autonomic testing – bladder scan, perianal sensation; spinal cord compression or cauda equina syndrome.
Look‑alike conditions: spinal cord compression, poliomyelitis, acute transverse myelitis, severe vitamin B12 deficiency.

qs.q: Which imaging modality is considered the study of choice to evaluate the degree of spinal cord compression and identify myelomalacia in a rheumatoid arthritis patient with neck pain?
qs.e: MRI is the study of choice to evaluate the degree of spinal cord compression and identify myelomalacia. CT scans are more useful to better delineate bony anatomy and for surgical planning.

qs.q: A 58-year-old woman with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis presents with progressive gait instability and hyperreflexia in the lower extremities. Which imaging modality is best suited to evaluate the extent of spinal cord compression and detect associated myelomalacia?
qs.e: Magnetic resonance imaging is the modality of choice for visualizing soft tissues, spinal cord compression, and intrinsic cord changes such as myelomalacia. Computed tomography provides superior visualization of bony architecture but lacks adequate soft-tissue contrast for the neural elements.

qs.q: In a patient experiencing acute spinal cord compression due to a plasmacytoma involving the thoracic spine, which emergency neurosurgical or oncological intervention may be required?
qs.e: Decompressive laminectomy, along with radiotherapy and chemotherapy, is part of the management for paraplegia resulting from spinal cord compression. Joint replacement is an orthopedic procedure meant for joint destruction rather than acute spinal cord compromise.
